title: Modules & Imports
lead: Each .xr file is a module. import/export must be top-level. The compiler builds a dependency DAG, topologically sorts it, and resolves selective imports to O(1) slot access at runtime.

sections.heading: Imports
sections.markdown: import declarations must appear at module top level. Bare identifiers resolve to stdlib; quoted paths resolve relative to the current file or project root. Dynamic import is not supported.

sections.heading: Exports
sections.markdown: export declarations must appear at module top level. export var is not supported — use export const. Re-exports (named and wildcard) aggregate submodule APIs.

sections.heading: Module graph & circular dependencies
sections.markdown: The compiler builds a module dependency DAG from all import declarations. Circular dependencies are a compile error. Modules initialize in topological order. Selective imports resolve to fixed module index + export slot at compile time.

sections.heading: Published Source definitions
sections.markdown:
Persistent Source checking receives only its owner's published Checked Program and registered bindings. Session inputs share a lexical scope while definitions retain birth modules and private visibility. Runtime receiving requires the actual Source map, exact specialized/Lowered Program proof and the same retained runtime Domain. Budgeted routes preserve birth slots and completed initialization. Actual stored-type roots receive existing type identities through acyclic arena ownership; equal shapes grant nothing, and values retain their birth type. Domain, publication, borrow and call checks remain separate. Old Cell reads/writes work in VM, native and mixed directions; ordinary Cell side effects survive candidate abort. Complete Class/Array operations, closures, full G2/G3 and P14 coordination remain unfinished. See compilation pipeline section17.50.

Array length, capacity, indexed reads, reserve, indexed writes and push use the actual data owner arena for element types and layouts after receiving-identity validation. Read-only ROOT_SLOT paths still refer to actual birth slots and check their original publication state. Paths retain the arena of each data edge and match static and actual container types by exact identity. Compact-leaf packing, unpacking, graph scans and destruction recover actual object headers. Existing erased Error views keep their Error tag and actual enum owner rather than becoming concrete enum handles. An Array allocated in the receiving arena can occupy a birth-arena compact element; writes to shared subtrees still copy before mutation and preserve independent copies. These type-coordinate changes never alter object headers or replace Domain or loan authority.

Deep function admission uses the actual function object's birth type arena during its callback, checking the real retained gate, Program, entry, complete declared bounds and capture roles. The receiver context and original work ledger remain in scope; nested admission and failed returns restore the receiver arena. Explicit weakening first validates exact receiving identity and complete signature bounds. When canonical identity is unchanged, a newly constructed carrier without a producer stamp remains in the actual birth arena and retains the real birth gate, entry and captures. A changed bound can construct a receiving carrier only from a receiving body proved by the ordinary compiler; matching shapes or copying producer permission cannot establish this correspondence.

An indirect call in the root execution stream selects its birth Program's entries, arena, admission context and Cell roles from the actual function gate. Each frame retains its own metadata coordinates. The same Call keeps the original executor, frame stack, depth, resumes, cancellation, cleanup and cumulative ledger; failed argument preparation and child exit restore parent metadata without copying or resetting work. VM call arguments, indirect callees, RETURN and generated C RETURN/THROW retain actual object headers rather than reconstructing old values from receiving numeric type identifiers. A worker call across Programs still needs independent sealed producer and invocation correspondence and rejects without it; RootNone or Sendable cannot replace that proof.

A host call to an old function selects its birth generation only for that execution. Subsequent Source storage receiving starts at the exact published generation, never treating the most recently executed old Program as published Source identity. Pending candidates, foreign Instances and stopped owners still reject. Escaped functions retain the actual birth Program and owned captures after Source, Instance and caller Program references die; final drop releases those leases. These semantics do not establish complete closure families, extra function/generic type roots, full G2/G3, paired REPL coordination or complete resource and safety qualification.

A public Source REPL owner owns the real Compiler, its Catalog and one cumulative Instance. A complete MEMORY input must match the namespace supplied at construction. Its once-parsed, authentic AST enters the same paired Source transaction. Only normal return publishes; compile or runtime failure publishes no new declarations and preserves ordinary prior-state writes and spent resources. Poll/wait/resume/cancel use the real runtime driver, and mutation during an output callback returns BUSY. Results, read values and diagnostics own their actual data and survive destruction of the entire REPL and Compiler. If actual candidate retirement still reports LIMIT/OOM, the observed event reports CLEANUP_FAILED and stops the owner while preserving the original terminal result; no fresh allowance is granted.

This public owner currently admits complete ordinary Source units. It does not yet elaborate tail-expression display, implicit it, rooted file inputs or CLI interaction. The original38 cases, extra generation cases, existing profile/TLS/scheduler behavior, complete fault/safety and SDK/provider gates remain separate completion requirements.
